correctness.rationale: The fixed-point parity recurrence rules out 11 and 0000. For odd lengths at least five, full cyclic occurrence contradicts parity of two one-positions, or creates a forbidden four-zero run. For even lengths, every full cyclic class has a unique desubstitution through μ, giving a reversible necklace bijection; base Lie counts at odd lengths one and three are computed exactly from the finite factor language. Consequently \(L(n)=2\) iff the odd part of n is 1 or 3. The standalone verifier checks 1–192 against exhaustive finite factor sets with a proved coverage prefix and independently agrees with the 2-adic fixed-point representation.

evidence: Cassaigne–Fici–Sciortino–Zamboni arXiv:1402.5843 §5.1 Example 1: ordinary cyclic complexity \(c_{\mathbf p}(2^k)=2\), where a class is counted if at least one rotation is present.
De Luca–Fici arXiv:2206.00995 §3: complete Lie complexity formula for Sturmian words, while the period-doubling word is a non-Sturmian Toeplitz word.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The known power-of-two ordinary cyclic-complexity claim has weaker orbit membership and no all-length triple-dyadic or zero-support classification. It cannot entail that every conjugate occurs, nor settle all lengths. A Sturmian classification cannot be applied to this non-Sturmian sequence.

evidence: Bell–Shallit: 2-automaticity is an existence theorem for a finite-state encoding of \(L_{\mathbf p}\), not an explicit specification of which lengths have nonzero Lie classes.
Cassaigne et al.: \(c_{\mathbf p}(2^k)=2\) is a weaker class-completeness condition on a sparse subsequence of lengths.
New proof: a reversible map [y] to [μ(y)] for all even lengths, odd-length obstruction via parity, and two exact odd base cases.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The claim adds the explicit all-positive-length Lie function, the classification of all corresponding cyclic words, and an all-even-length bijection. None follows as a stated corollary of the inspected general estimates or special ordinary-cyclic-complexity result without proving the additional desubstitution and parity lemmas.

evidence: Bell–Shallit arXiv:2102.03821v1 Definition (1), Theorem 1.4, §7: Lie complexity of automatic words is automatic, and concrete examples are Thue–Morse, its ternary variant, Cantor, Fibonacci and Tribonacci, not this morphism.
Li arXiv:2207.05859v1, Abstract and §§1,3–6: Rauzy-circuit and extended/prefix Lie-complexity frameworks, with no explicit period-doubling class count in inspected relevant material.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An equivalent statement would count rotation orbits whose entire conjugacy class belongs to the period-doubling factor language. The general automaticity and Rauzy formulations describe an abstract computable class but do not supply the precise support, constant value two, or representative families; no directly equivalent period-doubling theorem was located in the checked text. Non-detection alone is not a priority proof.

evidence: The primary Bell–Shallit Example 7.1 gives an explicit Thue–Morse table whose values differ at powers of two, not the period-doubling table.
The distinct Cassaigne et al. period-doubling table covers \(c_{\mathbf p}(2^k)=2\), not L_p(n) for all n.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No directly matching exact sequence/table covering the all-rotations count for every length was located in the examined publication searches. Published cyclic-complexity and Lie-complexity tables are not interchangeable. There remains a possibility of an obscure, unindexed OEIS or automatic-word computation.

No equivalent result appeared in the inspected material or actual research-record queries; residual priority risk is disclosed.

value.rationale: The Lie complexity of a canonical non-Sturmian automatic word is a motivated exact all-length invariant. The dyadic/triple-dyadic support, constant number two, and constructive identification of every cyclic class extend existing example tables. The new desubstitution bijection is structural and establishes an infinite family rather than a routine finite table or parameter substitution.
